question: Why did the static magnetic field promote single-crystal formation of sodium chlorate at high humidity?
expect: premise false: no measurable field effect; single crystals become more frequent at RH 59% independent of the applied field (abstract; Discussion)
rendered: The document does not state that the static magnetic field promoted single-crystal formation of sodium chlorate at high humidity. Instead, it states that higher humidity reduces the evaporation rate, weakens capillary-driven outward transport, and promotes single-crystal formation, whereas lower humidity favors coffee-ring and irregular deposition patterns. The document also states that the application of a static magnetic field of (290 ± 5) mT does not produce a measurable effect on deposition morphology or the relative fraction of single-crystal formations.
